acceptedAnswer.text: Composite resin placement is typically carried out under local anaesthetic, so the procedure itself should not be painful. Some patients experience mild sensitivity in the days following treatment, which usually settles without intervention. If you experience significant or prolonged discomfort after a composite restoration, it is worth informing your dental practice so the restoration can be reviewed. Individual experiences vary and your dentist will discuss what to expect during your consultation.

mainEntity.name: How long does a composite resin filling last?

acceptedAnswer.text: The lifespan of a composite resin restoration varies considerably depending on factors such as its size and location, the patient's bite, oral hygiene practices, and dietary habits. Composite fillings may last anywhere from five to ten or more years in suitable circumstances, though this cannot be guaranteed. Regular dental examinations allow your dentist to monitor restorations and advise on replacement or repair when clinically appropriate.

mainEntity.name: Can composite resin discolour over time?

acceptedAnswer.text: Composite resin can be susceptible to staining over time, particularly with frequent exposure to deeply coloured foods and drinks such as coffee, tea, red wine, and some berries, as well as tobacco products. Polishing during routine dental visits can help maintain surface smoothness and reduce staining, though some degree of colour change may occur over the lifetime of the restoration. Shade matching is performed at the outset, but the surrounding natural teeth may also change shade over time.

mainEntity.name: Is composite resin safe for use in teeth?

acceptedAnswer.text: Composite resin materials used in dental practice are subject to regulatory standards and have been extensively studied. They are considered safe for use in dental restorations. Patients with specific concerns about material composition — for example, those with documented sensitivities — are encouraged to discuss this with their dentist ahead of treatment, so that suitability can be assessed on an individual basis during a clinical consultation.

mainEntity.name: Does composite resin require special care after placement?

acceptedAnswer.text: No specific aftercare routine beyond standard good oral hygiene is required for composite resin restorations. Brushing twice daily with fluoride toothpaste, cleaning between teeth, and attending regular dental check-ups are the most important steps. It is advisable to avoid habits that may chip or crack the restoration — such as chewing on hard objects or using teeth as tools. If grinding or clenching is a concern, speak to your dentist about whether any additional protective measures may be appropriate for your circumstances.

mainEntity.name: How does composite resin compare to other filling materials?

acceptedAnswer.text: Composite resin offers aesthetic advantages over amalgam as it can be closely shade-matched to natural tooth colour. It also typically requires a more conservative preparation, preserving more healthy tooth structure. However, composite may be less durable than some ceramic or metal restorations in larger cavities or under significant biting forces. The most appropriate material for any individual depends on the clinical situation, and this is best determined through examination and discussion with a qualified dental professional.
